item.title: 2027: Soludo urges politicians to keep off places of worship
item.description: Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged politicians to keep politics away from places of worship, saying religious institutions should remain centres of spiritual growth and unity. Soludo made the call during a visit to the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention Deliverance Ministry Inc., Onitsha, to celebrate its 30th anniversary. The ministry was founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. He said: “Politicians, keep off places of worship! I do not do politics in the house of God. “I deliberately avoided church campaigns for six months before the last governorship election in Anambra. “My visit to religious institutions is usually motivated by my commitment to ecumenism and responsibility as the father of all in the state”. The governor described the anniversary as a significant milestone, noting that it marked maturity, preparation and a new phase in the ministry’s growth. He recalled that his first encounter with the ministry was during the demolition of part of its structure by the state government to facilitate the dredging of the Sakamori drainage channel. Soludo commended Odumeje for his contributions to charity and efforts towards societal development. He also acknowledged the cleric’s support for the state’s campaign against criminal idolatry and activities of illegal traditional spiritual practitioners. According to him, the advocacy, alongside the Anambra Homeland Security Law, has contributed to making the state safer. Responding, Odumeje pledged continued partnership with the state government to drive progress and development. item.title: Disu assures Abia residents of improved security
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has assured residents of Abia State of improved security, pledging that the Nigeria Police Force would intensify efforts to protect lives and property across the state. Disu gave the assurance during a courtesy visit to Governor Alex Otti at Government House, Umuahia, where he commended the governor for his sustained support to the police. The IGP, who said he had received positive reports from the Commissioner of Police and the Assistant Inspector-General of Police on the state government’s assistance to the Force, promised that the police would reciprocate the gesture through improved service delivery. “I want to thank you for all you have been doing for my officers. My Commissioner of Police has told me all you have been doing for us. The AIG too reiterated it. Thank you so much for it,” Disu said. He assured the governor that the police would remain committed to tackling security challenges and ensuring the safety of residents. “I will give you my word that we will continue to do our best to ensure proper policing so that people of the state will be able to sleep with their two eyes closed,” he said. Disu explained that his visit to Abia was primarily to attend the traditional marriage ceremony of his orderly, Victor Nnah Sunday, at Amangwu, Abaki-Ndoki, in Ukwa East Local Government Area. He, however, said he considered it necessary to pay homage to Otti, as the state’s Chief Security Officer, before proceeding to the wedding venue. Responding, Otti commended the police leadership for its professionalism and prompt response to the state government’s requests for assistance in addressing security challenges. “Thank you for what you do for the country. Thank you for the professionalism of the Force and for making everyone realise that the safety and security of the people is paramount. “We have had instances where we called upon you and you responded swiftly,” the governor said. Otti also praised the promotion of the immediate past Commissioner of Police in Abia to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police, describing his service in the state as professional and tactful. He said the former police commissioner demonstrated commitment in handling security matters, adding that although the state would have preferred to retain him, his elevation was a welcome development. “He demonstrated professionalism and tact in the discharge of his duties. If not that it is a promotion, we would have resisted it, but we believe it is good for him to move on,” Otti said. The governor expressed optimism that the officer would sustain his relationship with Abia despite his new position. Otti also congratulated the IGP’s orderly on his traditional marriage, recalling that he had met him during an earlier encounter with the police chief. item.title: 2027: Atiku promises to end insecurity if elected
item.description: By Nabilu Balarabe The Presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar has promised to tackle insurgency and other forms of insecurity, if voted in the 2027 Presidential election. Atiku made the promise in Potiskum on Sunday during the party’s campaign rally. He also promised to provide an enabling environment for youths to develop careers in all areas of their interest. “Whatever you want to do, my administration will support you. But we will not allow all acts of violence,” he said. Abubakar said he would revive the economy by providing affordable fuel, electricity and cutting taxes. He, however, said all these could only be achieved if voters came out en-mass to vote for him in the forthcoming election. Abubakar advised the electorate to vote wisely for candidates that would better their lot and reject corrupt and selfish politicians. “Vote the ADC for your future and the future of your children. We are ready to serve you in every way we can,” Atiku said. In his remarks, the ADC National Secretary, Mr Rauf Aregbesola, thanked the people of Yobe for their warm reception to the party’s candidates. He urged the electorate to vote for change and ensure that due process was followed in counting and collation of votes cast. item.title: One firefighter injured as hoodlums attack crew in Abuja
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — One firefighter was injured after suspected hoodlums attacked a Federal Fire Service crew responding to a fire emergency at 7th Avenue, Gwarinpa, Abuja, at the weekend. The suspected perpetrators have reportedly been arrested and are under investigation following the incident. The Federal Capital Territory Command of the service condemned the attack in a statement issued by its Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Fire Anyam Barnabas. The statement said the firefighters, attached to the Kubwa Metropolitan Fire Station, were responding to a distress call from a resident, Mrs Amina, at about 10am when they came under attack. On arrival at the scene, the crew were reportedly pelted with stones by suspected hoodlums, leaving one firefighter injured. The injured officer was immediately taken to a hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the Galadima Police Station, while the suspects were said to be under investigation. The Controller of the Federal Fire Service, FCT Command, Mohammed Anas, expressed displeasure over what he described as persistent attacks on firefighters while carrying out their statutory responsibilities. He warned that anyone who attacked or obstructed firefighters at emergency scenes would face the consequences of the law. Anas urged residents of the FCT to appreciate and support firefighters, particularly during emergency operations, and called on those involved in such acts to desist. He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to prompt and effective emergency response across the territory, stressing that firefighters must be allowed to perform their duties without intimidation, harassment or attacks. The controller also appealed to residents to cooperate with emergency responders and provide the necessary support to enable them to save lives and protect property. item.title: Igbokoda Crash: NAF recovers black box, holds memorial November 26
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has confirmed the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) from the site of the October 5 aircraft crash at Igbokoda, Ondo State, announcing plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony for the victims on November 26. The ceremony will take place at the National Military Cemetery, Abuja, in honour of the personnel and other victims who lost their lives in the NAF 931 aircraft accident. NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the event would provide an opportunity for bereaved families, colleagues, friends and members of the Air Force community to pay their last respects. He said the ceremony would also serve as a formal expression of the Service’s respect and remembrance for those who died in the incident. On the recovery of the aircraft’s black box, Ejodame said the CVR, alongside other aircraft fragments and relevant evidence, had been retrieved from the crash site. He explained that data recovered from the voice recorder was being analysed and was expected to contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident. According to him, the investigation is progressing in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA). The Air Force reiterated its commitment to ensuring that the investigation was conducted in accordance with the highest standards of professionalism, transparency, accountability and responsibility, while supporting the independent technical processes required to establish the cause of the crash. Ejodame further disclosed that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while the identification process for the recovered remains was ongoing. He said the operation had been particularly challenging because of the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth to which some of the aircraft wreckage had penetrated the ground. The NAF spokesman added that the Service was engaging relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery exercise and ensure appropriate remediation after its completion. He said the Air Force recognised the grief of the bereaved families and remained committed to providing them with sustained support throughout the difficult period. The Service also appreciated the cooperation of relevant agencies, host communities and other stakeholders who had continued to support the recovery and investigation efforts. The NAF assured the public of its commitment to a thorough investigation, responsible environmental management and the dignified remembrance of all those who lost their lives. item.title: Sanwo-Olu rewards Flamingos, coaches with N10m each

In addition to the cash reward, each player received an iPhone 18 Pro Max and bespoke outfits in recognition of the team’s achievement as the first African side to win the global tournament. The governor said the gesture was in recognition of the team’s landmark victory on the global stage, which has attracted widespread acclaim across Nigeria and the African continent. The reception provided an opportunity for the Lagos State Government to celebrate the players and technical crew for bringing honour to Nigeria and making history in women’s football. item.title: Sanusi, Ladoja warn against politicising traditional institutions
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, have called for national healing, peaceful coexistence and stronger bonds among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups, warning against the politicisation of traditional institutions. The two traditional rulers spoke on Sunday in Ibadan when Sanusi paid a courtesy visit to Ladoja at his palace in Oke-Aremo, where they stressed the need for traditional institutions to remain above partisan interests and serve as instruments of reconciliation, mutual understanding and national unity. Sanusi, who was in Ibadan to honour an invitation from the League of Imams and Alfas in South-West Nigeria, said his visit reflected his belief in a country where ethnic, religious and political differences would not determine relationships among citizens. He described the engagement as one of the positive developments needed to bridge Nigeria’s regional and cultural divides, stressing that national unity, progress and prosperity could only be achieved when people from different backgrounds deliberately reached out to one another. The Emir said although other engagements had emerged, he considered it important to honour his earlier commitment to attend the conference, even if his participation would be brief. “We fixed this date a long time ago, and even though other events came, we considered it important to honour our promise to appear at the conference, even if it is for a brief period, because they have been expecting me to come. “This invitation is part of the positive developments we have been yearning for to build a bridge where Nigerians from different parts of the country reach out to each other and come together in the interest of the unity, the progress and the prosperity of our dear nation,” he said. Sanusi also apologised for the delay in visiting Ladoja following his appointment and coronation, explaining that certain circumstances had prevented him from attending earlier. He congratulated Ladoja on his ascension to the throne of his forebears and prayed for divine protection, a long and peaceful reign, as well as prosperity for Ibadanland and Nigeria. The Emir described the courtesy visit as necessary, given the longstanding relationship between the two traditional institutions and their respective communities. Reflecting on his relationship with Ibadan, Sanusi recalled his longstanding connections with the ancient city dating back to his days at First Bank, his association with the late Aare Musulumi of Yorubaland, Alhaji Abdulazeez Arisekola Alao, and his subsequent tenure as Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria. He said Ibadan had remained a familiar destination over the years, adding that he had maintained close relationships with several indigenes of the city. item.title: NDC candidate in Kwara pledges N120,000 minimum wage for workers
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kwara, Prof. Abdulmumin Ajia, has pledged a minimum wage of N120,000 for workers in the state. Ajia made the pledge on Sunday in Ilorin while unveiling the NDC’s 2027 Gubernatorial Campaign Council manifesto, tagged ‘Forward Kwara Agenda’. He proposed a N120,000 public-service minimum wage benchmark and a cost-of-living adjustment framework for workers and pensioners. He said his administration would verify the payroll, assess the financial implications, consult labour unions and publish an implementation and funding timetable. On pensioners, Ajia promised to verify outstanding gratuities and publish a schedule for settling validated arrears. He also pledged to establish a predictable payment timetable for newly due pension obligations. Ajia said he entered the governorship race to make public institutions work reliably for all Kwarans, regardless of political affiliation. “I am running to make public institutions work that way. If entrusted with office, I will serve people who support me, people who oppose me and people who have never attended a political meeting,” he said. He said his experience as a teacher, researcher and university administrator had taught him to ask critical questions, examine evidence and take responsibility for results. Ajia, who led a School of Business and mentored young people, said his visits home exposed him to the challenges facing unemployed graduates. He said many young people could hardly predict when fair employment opportunities would become available. According to him, government has a responsibility to ensure that citizens understand how to access assistance, eligibility requirements and appeal procedures. He said access to public services should not depend on personal relationships with the governor. Ajia said the Forward Kwara Agenda outlined six areas of governance, anchored on stronger institutions, greater opportunities and shared prosperity. On security, he said farmers should access their farms, children should travel safely to school and traders should return home safely from markets. NAN reports that the event attracted hundreds of NDC stakeholders from the state’s 16 local government areas. item.title: ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach
item.description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp praised Xavi Hernandez on Sunday, saying the new Netherlands coach already had the Dutch playing in his own image after just five games in charge. Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday’s meeting between the two old rivals, Klopp pointed to Friday’s 7-0 thumping of Greece in Amsterdam and said the former midfielder had made an impression. Considered among the best midfielders in the history of the game, Xavi formed the core of a possession-dominant Barcelona side who won four Champions League titles. He also won the World Cup with Spain. “They simply played some electric football,” Klopp said, adding: “Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football… “He’s a coach who really pushes his approach to the limit. And that’s exciting. I always loved playing against teams who play like this.” Third in the group with only the top two reaching the quarter-finals, Germany will need to beat the Netherlands to give themselves a chance. “They’re a team who really come alive in European football,” Klopp said of the Netherlands. “It’s one of the fiercest rivalries in football. It’s a great honour for me.” Appointed in August, the Spaniard said he was beginning to understand the nature of the rivalry with Germany. “Now I can understand more because I’m here and I feel this kind of rivalry. It will be a really good test for us,” Xavi said. In his press conference, Xavi deflected Klopp’s praise and said the Netherlands’ big win over Greece was down to his players. “It’s not Xavi-football. It’s all about the players. They are the most important. I don’t need to convince them to play this style of football, they have the capacity to play like the last game. Germany and the Netherlands played out a 1-1 draw in Amsterdam in September, the first match in charge for both Klopp and Xavi. Xavi said he would try and do the unexpected on Monday, but acknowledged it would not be easy against the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach. “It’s difficult to surprise a coach like Jurgen Klopp,” Xavi said. “He’s one of the best coaches in the past few years. And it’s an honour to come up against him tomorrow.” Vanguard News The post ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: NDC accuses Tinubu of prioritising campaign propaganda over budgets
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of prioritising campaign propaganda and political patronage over funding critical sectors of the economy, alleging that the huge spending on political publicity explains the poor implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 budgets. The opposition party challenged the Federal Government to publish verifiable figures showing how much had been released for critical capital projects and administrative subventions in the three fiscal years, compared with expenditure on political advertisements and patronage. The NDC made the allegations in a statement signed on Sunday by the Spokesperson of its National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, titled, “Dear Mr. President: The Huge Cost of Your Campaign Propaganda Testifies to Why You Failed to Adequately Fund 2024, 2025 and 2026 Budgets.” The party said its assessment of what it described as a barrage of political advertisements, donations, vehicles, laptops, sewing machines, food items and other gifts distributed by groups and individuals claiming to support Tinubu had raised questions about the administration’s spending priorities. It alleged that despite increased government revenue following the removal of fuel subsidy and higher taxation, critical social and physical infrastructure, national security and citizens’ welfare had not received adequate funding. Ikokwu said: “For instance, despite the palpable insecurity confronting the nation, only about seven per cent of the Defence Capital Budget was reportedly released in 2025. “Even more disturbing was when the Minister of Health reported that only ₦36 million out of the ₦218 billion allocated to Health Capital expenditure was released in the same 2025.” The party argued that the alleged low releases for defence and health raised questions about the government’s commitment to addressing insecurity and improving public services. It also expressed concern over the implementation of the 2026 budget, which it claimed had received inadequate attention, and accused the APC of devoting substantial resources to campaign publicity and political patronage ahead of the 2027 elections. Questioning the administration’s spending priorities, Ikokwu asked how a government benefiting from fuel subsidy removal and increased taxation could plead a lack of funds for national security, healthcare, education, federal roads and the welfare of ordinary Nigerians while political activities appeared to attract substantial resources. The NDC also alleged that several state governments, particularly those it claimed had been pressured into joining the APC, had poor records of budget implementation but had sufficient resources for campaign propaganda. item.title: Gridlock as multiple trailers crash on Lagos-Ibadan Expressway
item.description: …Inward-Lagos carriageway blocked at Kara Bridge By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Traffic was brought to a standstill on Sunday evening following a multiple-trailer crash around Kara Bridge, near Ibafo, on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The accident blocked the inward-Lagos carriageway, leaving motorists stranded as emergency responders and traffic officials battled to clear the wreckage. A trailer with an unknown registration number was seen overturned on its side, with its container crushed and contents scattered across the road, while other trailers were rammed into one another behind it. Officials of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, and other emergency personnel were at the scene directing traffic, controlling onlookers and coordinating clearance operations. A heavy-duty tow truck and payloader were also deployed to remove the wrecked vehicles and restore traffic movement. The crash attracted dozens of onlookers, while vehicles on the opposite carriageway moved slowly as motorists attempted to catch a glimpse of the accident scene. Efforts to clear the affected carriageway were ongoing as of press time. Motorists travelling towards Lagos from Ibafo, Mowe and adjoining areas were advised to exercise patience, drive cautiously around the scene and explore alternative routes where possible. The cause of the crash and whether there were casualties had yet to be established as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Mammoth crowd welcomes Wali as Buni empowers over 500 youths, women in Yobe South
item.description: There was a mammoth crowd in Gadaka, Fika Local Government Area of Yobe State, on Thursday as the state government distributed empowerment items to over 500 youths and women across Yobe South Senatorial District (Zone B). The beneficiaries, drawn from the four local government areas in the zone, received motorcycles, tricycles (Jega) and sewing machines. The empowerment is aimed at promoting economic inclusion, supporting small businesses and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities. Beneficiaries and stakeholders at the event expressed appreciation for the intervention, saying it would boost economic activities at the grassroots. They also reaffirmed their support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Governor Mai Mala Buni and the All Progressives Congress (APC), citing investments in road infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and peacebuilding across their communities. Speaking at the event, the APC governorship candidate in the state, Hon. Baba Mallam Wali, commended Governor Buni’s economic empowerment initiatives and pledged to sustain and consolidate them if elected in the 2027 general elections. Wali said the programme would be expanded to reach more youths and women across the state. Party leaders at the event also reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening party unity and working for the success of the APC at all levels, from the State House of Assembly to the Presidency.

item.title: 2027 Grammys Nominations To Be Announced Monday
item.description: Nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, scheduled to hold in February 2027, will be announced on Monday, November 16, with Nigerian music fans able to follow the presentation from 1:45 p.m. West African Time (WAT). The Recording Academy will unveil nominees across all 100 categories during a special presentation led by its Chief Executive Officer, Harvey Mason Jr., and Chair of its Board of Trustees, Dr Chelsey Green. The announcement will begin at 7:45 a.m. Eastern Time (1:45 p.m. WAT), while the complete list of nominees is expected to be published around 9 a.m. Eastern Time (3 p.m. WAT). The presentation will be streamed live on Grammy.com and the official Grammys YouTube channel, with additional coverage on ABC’s Good Morning America. New Categories The 2027 edition introduces five new award categories, bringing the total number of categories to 100. They are Best Asian Pop Music Performance, Best Latin Song, Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance, and Best Traditional Folk Album. The eligibility period for the awards covers recordings released between August 31, 2025, and August 28, 2026. item.title: Bloody Spit: Ghana Waste Dump Poses Health, Environmental ‘Crisis’
item.description: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana’s capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water. At Agbogbloshie, a district on the Korle Lagoon delta, thousands of tonnes of refuse have accumulated over decades, overwhelming the fragile wetlands overlooking a slum of around 80,000 residents, many of them migrants and traders. For scrap dealer James Hassan, a 31-year-old Liberian immigrant, it is both his home and livelihood. Without gloves or a mask, he sifts daily through piles of unwanted electronics and metal for scraps to sell. The skin on his palms is thickened and scarred from cuts and rashes but he has become accustomed to the pain and discomfort. “I have headaches and coughs after long days under the sun, but I have never sought medical care. I feel they are normal,” he told AFP. Environmental health experts say that workers are exposed to toxic metals and chemicals through skin cuts, inhaling waste smoke and dust. Waste collectors dig through piles of waste at the Agbogbloshie dumpsite in Accra, on September 28, 2026. Photo by NIPAH DENNIS / AFP While no study as yet links specific diseases to Agbogbloshie’s pollution, “the cumulative contamination raises concern even if precise causal chains remain unquantified,” epidemiologist Reginald Quansah, of the University of Ghana, said. Global Pipeline Of Waste Waste management is a prominent theme at the COP31 climate talks, which began in Turkey on Monday. Agbogbloshie’s refuse comes largely from beyond Ghana’s borders. Accra’s huge second-hand clothing market has imports from Europe, North America and Asia — but often with a troubling byproduct. “A lot of clothes that are shipped into Ghana come as waste,” Greenpeace Africa’s head of investigations Samuel Quashie-Idun told AFP. Greenpeace estimates that 15 million used garments arrive in Ghana each week. Even after traders extract what they can sell, roughly half ends up as “dead waste” dumped on beaches and fields or burned, it said. One study Greenpeace cited put Ghana’s used clothing imports at over 110,000 tonnes in 2022. For the country’s 35 million people, “these volumes far exceed local demand and… burdens waste systems,” Quashie-Idun said. Greenpeace found that 89 percent of sampled “dead” garments contained petrochemical fibres such as polyester, which shed microplastics as they decay, and release carcinogens hundreds of times above safe levels in smoke when the textiles are burned. “This is not just an environmental crisis… it’s also a human health crisis,” said Hellen Kahaso Dena, Greenpeace’s plastics project expert. ‘Fashion Waste Dumping Ground’ “The global north is effectively using Ghana as a dumping ground for fashion waste,” she told AFP. item.title: Cabo Verde Votes In Presidential Election As Incumbent Seeks Second Term
item.description: Cabo Verde voted for a new president on Sunday, with incumbent Jose Maria Neves favoured to win a second term as head of state of the West African archipelago renowned for its democratic stability. He is facing the country’s first woman candidate, Joana Rosa Amado, among other contenders. Voting started at 0900 GMT and ends at 1900 GMT. Provisional results are expected overnight. “I’ve voted. Now I’m going to mass, and I believe everything will go well — normally and with civic-mindedness,” Adilia Gomes, 55, told AFP after casting her ballot in the capital, Praia. “Everything went normally despite a few minutes’ delay in the opening of my polling station,” added another voter, Claudino Semedo. Nearly 420,000 people are eligible to vote. The election is being watched by about 150 observers from the Economic Community of West African States, the African Union and European Union. A supporter of Cape Verde’s President and presidential candidate Jose Maria Neves waves a flag bearing his image during a campaign rally in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on October 30, 2026.(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) Cabo Verde, located in the Atlantic Ocean about 600 kilometres (375 miles) off the coast of Senegal, comprises 10 volcanic islands and is an increasingly popular tourist destination. It made world headlines this year when its national football team reached the knockout stages in its first World Cup, and when a cruise ship containing people with hantavirus docked off its shores. Stability, Hospitality Unlike several of its West African neighbours where presidential elections have been tense in recent years, Cabo Verde is known for its political stability and good governance. It is considered a model of democracy in Africa, with strong economic growth. A voter queues at a polling station during Cape Verde’s presidential election in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on November 15, 2026(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) The country is known for its “morabeza” (“hospitality”, in local creole), openness, and carnivals. It also has its own style of music. According to the Mo Ibrahim Foundation 2026 index on global governance, Cabo Verde ranks third out of 54 countries on the continent. Politically, it has a semi-presidential system in which the executive is dominated by the prime minister. The president does not govern but acts more as an arbiter, working to guarantee unity and uphold the constitution. The head of state appoints the prime minister based on the results of legislative elections and represents the country abroad.
